This regex validates a password-style string. Here's the breakdown:

```
^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z]).{8,}$
```

| Part | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `^` | Start of string |
| `(?=.*[a-z])` | **Lookahead**: assert there's at least one lowercase letter somewhere ahead |
| `(?=.*[A-Z])` | **Lookahead**: assert there's at least one uppercase letter somewhere ahead |
| `.{8,}` | Match 8 or more of any character (except newline) |
| `$` | End of string |

## What `Property 'x' does not exist on type 'Y'` means

TypeScript is telling you: **you're trying to access a property (`x`) that isn't part of the known shape of the value you have (type `Y`).** TypeScript tracks what properties every value is allowed to have, and when you reach for one it can't guarantee exists, it stops you at compile time rather than letting you hit `undefined` at runtime.
